entities.evidence: The man explicitly gives his wife the name חַוָּה (Eve). The verse identifies her as the mother of all the living.

review.translation: [Then|0] [the man|1] [called|0] [the name of|2] [his wife|3] [Eve|4], [because|5] [she|6] [was|7] [the mother of|8] [all|9] [the living|10].

analysis.evidence: הָאָדָם is the subject. שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ means “his wife’s name,” and חַוָּה supplies the name he gave her.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: הָאָדָם is the subject of וַיִּקְרָא. He names his wife (אִשְׁתּוֹ) Eve (חַוָּה), which identifies him as the first man in the narrative.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ means “the name of his wife.” The man gives her the name חַוָּה (Eve).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ, “the name of his wife,” the suffix refers to הָאָדָם, the man who names his wife חַוָּה (Eve).
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ חַוָּה says that the man named his wife Eve. The following כִּי clause explains the name through wordplay with חָי in אֵם כָּל־חָי, “mother of all the living,” supporting the article’s association with חיה.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular personal name without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name given to the man's wife.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason the man named his wife חַוָּה: she was the mother of all living.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected causal conjunction without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הִוא refers to Eve, just named חַוָּה. It is the subject of the feminine singular verb הָיְתָה in “because she was the mother of all living.”
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person feminine singular, written הִוא and read הִיא.

analysis.evidence: הָיְתָה agrees with הִוא “she” and links it to the predicate אֵם כָּל־חָי “the mother of all living.” The כִּי clause gives the reason for the name חַוָּה.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: אֵם is in construct with כָּל חָי. The clause כִּי הִוא הָיְתָה אֵם כָּל חָי explains Eve’s name by saying that she was the mother of all the living.
כָּל governs the singular חָי, “living one.” The phrase אֵם כָּל חָי calls Eve the mother of every living person.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֵם כָּל חָי, “mother of all the living,” כָּל gives חָי collective scope. The phrase explains the name חַוָּה by identifying her as the mother of everyone who lives.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally, with pausal vocalization חָי.
